facts.fact_text: On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in the city of Malatya.
On 8 March 2005 the applicants took part in International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya, according to the Government's submissions.
Police officers dragged a number of persons, including four of the applicants, into waiting police vehicles.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
The second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, was sprayed with tear gas during the events of 8 March 2005.
The four arrested applicants were taken to a police station on 8 March 2005.

On 8 March 2005 the Malatya prosecutor filed an indictment with the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance and brought criminal proceedings against the four applicants and the remaining five persons who had been arrested together with the applicants.

The criminal proceedings brought on 8 March 2005 against the four applicants and the five other arrested persons were for insulting the police officers and contravening the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
According to the Government's submissions, the demonstrations at the International Women's Day celebrations in Malatya on 8 March 2005 hindered the flow of traffic.
According to the Government's submissions, a police chief warned the participants on 8 March 2005 that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.

According to the Government's submissions, the police chief made several unsuccessful attempts to tell the participants that the manner in which they were conducting their demonstration was unlawful because they were impeding the flow of traffic.
According to the Government's submissions, the group of demonstrators insisted on blocking the street and continued with their demonstration on 8 March 2005.
During the International Women's Day celebrations on 8 March 2005 in Malatya, the police chief warned the participants that no prior permission had been obtained for the gathering.
The first applicant, Ms Nihal Pekaslan, told the police chief that the applicable legislation required no prior permission for the gathering.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers sprayed the crowds with tear gas.
In the course of dragging persons into police vehicles, police officers hit some of the crowd, including four of the applicants.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the four applicants who had been hit by police officers had a number of injuries on their bodies.
According to medical reports drawn up on 8 March 2005, the injuries sustained by the four applicants rendered them unable to work for periods of between one and three days.
The part of the video footage where the police officers used force and arrested the applicants does not feature in the footage submitted to the Court.
It can be seen from the video footage that before they were arrested the applicants drew the police officers' attention to a circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004.
In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, the Ministry urges police officers to respect certain rights and freedoms, including freedom of expression and assembly.

In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, the Ministry reminds police officers that rights and freedoms including freedom of expression and assembly can only be restricted in limited circumstances.
In the circular issued by the Ministry of the Interior on 11 June 2004, police officers are urged to show restraint when faced with demonstrations.

According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Ms Nihal Pekaslan had four ecchymosed areas measuring between one and five centimetres on both forearms and on the left hand, and grazes on both forearms and on the left hand.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Ms Nihal Pekaslan's injuries prevented her from working for three days.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Ms Kıvanç Pekaslan had an ecchymosed area measuring 2 x 2 centimetres on the inside of the right arm.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Ms Kıvanç Pekaslan's injury prevented her from working for one day.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Mr İbrahim Bozay had two ecchymosed areas each measuring 1 x 1 centimetre on the forehead.

According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Mr İbrahim Bozay had two ecchymosed grazes on one of the fingers of the right hand and on the right forearm, measuring 1 x 1 and 2 x 2 centimetres respectively.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Mr İbrahim Bozay's injuries prevented him from working for one day.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, the doctor observed two ecchymosed areas measuring 1 x 1 and 2 x 1 centimetres on the insides of both arms of Ms Leyla Bozay.
According to the medical report of 8 March 2005, Ms Leyla Bozay's injuries prevented her from working for one day.
In their objection, the applicants pointed out that according to the applicable legislation, no prior permission was necessary to hold demonstrations.
On 2 June 2005 the Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance acquitted the four applicants and the remaining defendants.
The Malatya Criminal Court of First Instance held on 2 June 2005 that there was no evidence to show that the four applicants had put up resistance against the police officers.

On 8 March 2005 the second applicant, Ms Refika Meltem İspir, lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers who, she alleged, had sprayed her and her daughter with tear gas.
On 11 March 2005 the remaining four applicants lodged an official complaint with the prosecutor against the police officers allegedly responsible for the ill-treatment.
On 12 May 2005 the Malatya prosecutor decided not to prosecute the police officers involved in the events of 8 March 2005.
The objection filed by the applicants against the Malatya prosecutor's decision not to prosecute the police officers was rejected by the Elazığ Assize Court on 28 July 2005.
